title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 11-12
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 11 to 12 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'अजः सर्वेश्वरः सिद्धः सिद्धिः सर्वादिरच्युतः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 11 to 12 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 11 to 12.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 11 to 12** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **अजः सर्वेश्वरः सिद्धः सिद्धिः सर्वादिरच्युतः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**अजः सर्वेश्वरः सिद्धः सिद्धिः सर्वादिरच्युतः । वृषाकपिरमेयात्मा सर्वयोगविनिःसृतः ॥** **वसुर्वसुमनाः सत्यः समात्मा सम्मितः समः । अमोघः पुण्डरीकाक्षो वृषकर्मा वृषाकृतिः ॥**

He is unborn and the Lord of all. Perfect himself and the giver of perfection, the beginning of everything is that God of gods. He never slips, he is dharma itself, and every path of yoga flows from him. He is the true wealth, kind of heart, the truth itself. The same in all, perfectly balanced, is that God of gods. His work never fails; lotus-eyed, he is the one who upholds dharma.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 11 to 12 mean?
faq.a: He is unborn and the Lord of all. Perfect himself and the giver of perfection, the beginning of everything is that God of gods. He never slips, he is dharma itself, and every path of yoga flows from him. He is the true wealth, kind of heart, the truth itself. The same in all, perfectly balanced, is that God of gods. His work never fails; lotus-eyed, he is the one who upholds dharma.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
